newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Oil product jetty at India's Kandla port closed.
newsitem.headline: Oil product jetty at India's Kandla port closed.

text.p: One of Kandla port's three oil products receiving jetties was closed on Tuesday after it was damaged following a collision between two vessels, traders in Singapore said on Wednesday.
Kandla is on the west coast of India.
Traders later said that a second jetty had also been closed as a result of the accident.
The first jetty is not expected to be operational for up to two months, while the second may be down for up to four months, traders said.
Traders said two tankers, the Jag Prayog and the J.N. Vyas, were in a collision between the two jetties.
They said the Indian oil industry might seek government approval for priority handling of diesel tankers so that the Kandla-Batinda pipeline and rail and road movements out of Kandla do not suffer.
Traders said that there are about 18 tankers waiting to discharge diesel at the Kandla port.
The berth congestion has already led India to reduce its diesel imports substantially over the past few months.
